authority: CEO Round 140: 'Construct the strongest multi-reference obviousness case against C2. The enemy is: Can I combine the relevant prior art and arrive at this invention without inventive insight?'

corrected_limitation_taxonomy.rationale: Per CEO Round 140: 'Separate CLAIM_LIMITATION from ENGINEERING_REQUIREMENT from VALIDATION_REQUIREMENT from IMPLEMENTATION_OPTION. Do not allow implementation options such as MEMS to become artificial novelty limitations.'

CL1.description: Continuous pressure sensing in a CSF shunt system

CL2.description: Endovascular sensor placement (venous anatomy, not traditional VP shunt)

CL4.description: Differential pressure measurement (CSF pressure - venous pressure)

CL5.description: Temporal signature classification algorithm (distinguishing obstruction from posture/cough/drift by temporal pattern)

CL6.description: Obstruction detection from the differential pressure temporal signature

ER1.description: Implantable sensor form factor fitting eShunt anatomy

ER2.description: Signal processing capability for temporal analysis

VR2.description: Clinical validation of obstruction detection accuracy

IO1.description: MEMS sensor technology (one possible implementation; NOT a claim limitation unless the invention structurally requires MEMS)

corrected_limitation_taxonomy.key_correction: MEMS (previously L4) is now IO1 (IMPLEMENTATION_OPTION), not a claim limitation. 5-year biocompatibility (previously L7) is now VR1 (VALIDATION_REQUIREMENT), not a claim limitation. This prevents C2 from 'winning' novelty by adding arbitrary implementation details.

anchor_reference.title: Ventricular shunt system and method
anchor_reference.role: ANCHOR — closest prior art for CSF shunt pressure monitoring
anchor_reference.discloses: VP shunt + pressure sensor on catheter assembly + passive LC resonant circuit + wireless/ex-vivo RF interrogation + pressure indicative of ventricular pressure + shunt malfunction diagnosis
anchor_reference.missing_from_C2: Endovascular anatomy (CL2, CL3), differential pressure (CL4), temporal signature analysis (CL5), obstruction algorithm (CL6)

US10413710B2.title: Pressure reference assembly for body fluid drainage system
US10413710B2.role: DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE — teaches two reference lines with flexible regions for differential pressure sensing in body fluid drainage
US10413710B2.key_disclosure: A first reference line with a first flexible region configured to sense pressure, and a second reference line with a second flexible region configured to sense pressure — this is a DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE measurement system for body fluid drainage (e.g., CSF shunt).
US10413710B2.motivation_to_combine: HIGH — a POSITA working on shunt pressure monitoring (field of US8870787) would be motivated to use differential pressure measurement (taught by US10413710) to improve obstruction detection accuracy. The problem being solved: absolute pressure alone cannot distinguish obstruction from other pressure changes. Differential pressure provides better specificity.

US10806352B2.title: Wireless vascular monitoring implant
US10806352B2.role: VASCULAR IMPLANT — teaches wireless pressure sensing implant deployed in patient vasculature (vena cava specifically mentioned)
US10806352B2.key_disclosure: A wireless vascular monitoring implant adapted to be deployed in a patient vasculature, positioned at a monitoring location in a vascular lumen (specifically mentions vena cava), with a resilient sensor construct forming a variable inductance resonant circuit.
US10806352B2.addresses_C2_limitation: CL2 (endovascular sensor placement — specifically venous anatomy)
US10806352B2.motivation_to_combine: MODERATE — US10806352 teaches placing a wireless pressure sensor in the vena cava. A POSITA working on CSF-venous shunt monitoring would recognize that venous pressure sensing is needed for the differential measurement. However, the primary purpose of US10806352 is cardiovascular monitoring, not CSF shunt monitoring — the motivation to adapt it to CSF shunt context requires cross-domain insight.

US10166375B2.title: Body fluid drainage system
US10166375B2.role: DRAINAGE SYSTEM — teaches body fluid drainage with valve device (shunt context)
US10166375B2.key_disclosure: A body fluid drainage system with catheter and valve device configured to change resistance to flow.
US10166375B2.addresses_C2_limitation: Context — confirms body fluid drainage (CSF shunt) as the field

strongest_section_103_attack.combination: US8870787B2 (CSF shunt pressure sensor) + US10413710B2 (differential pressure reference assembly) + US10806352B2 (vascular/venous pressure implant) + eShunt anatomy (CereVasc US20240299714A1)

what_each_reference_contributes.US8870787: CSF shunt system + pressure sensor + wireless interrogation + shunt malfunction diagnosis objective
what_each_reference_contributes.US10413710: Differential pressure measurement using two reference lines in body fluid drainage context
what_each_reference_contributes.US10806352: Endovascular/venous placement of wireless pressure sensor (vena cava mentioned)

C2_limitations_addressed_by_combination.CL1_continuous_pressure_sensing: ADDRESSED by US8870787 (pressure sensor in shunt, wireless interrogation)
C2_limitations_addressed_by_combination.CL2_endovascular_sensor: PARTIALLY ADDRESSED by US10806352 (vascular implant, vena cava placement)
C2_limitations_addressed_by_combination.CL3_eShunt_anatomy: ADDRESSED by CereVasc eShunt patent (endovascular transvenous subarachnoid access)
C2_limitations_addressed_by_combination.CL4_differential_pressure: ADDRESSED by US10413710 (two reference lines for differential pressure in body fluid drainage)
C2_limitations_addressed_by_combination.CL5_temporal_signature: NOT ADDRESSED — no reference teaches temporal pattern classification for distinguishing obstruction from posture/cough/drift
C2_limitations_addressed_by_combination.CL6_obstruction_algorithm: PARTIALLY ADDRESSED — US8870787 mentions shunt malfunction diagnosis but no specific algorithm

attack_assessment.anticipation_102: NO — no single reference discloses all limitations
attack_assessment.obviousness_103: MODERATE TO STRONG — the combination of US8870787 + US10413710 + US10806352 + eShunt addresses CL1-CL4 and partially CL6. The motivation to combine is MODERATE: a POSITA working on shunt pressure monitoring would be motivated to add differential measurement (US10413710) and vascular placement (US10806352) to the eShunt anatomy. However, the KEY MISSING ELEMENT is CL5 (temporal signature classification).
attack_assessment.missing_element: CL5 — temporal signature classification algorithm. No reference in the citation network teaches distinguishing obstruction from posture, cough, or drift based on temporal patterns of the differential pressure signal. This is C2's potentially most defensible novelty.
attack_assessment.reasonable_expectation_of_success: MODERATE for CL1-CL4. LOW for CL5 — temporal signature classification requires signal processing expertise and clinical insight about CSF pressure dynamics that is not taught by any combination of the prior art.
attack_assessment.teaching_away: US8870787's passive LC circuit (requiring external interrogation) teaches away from continuous implantable monitoring. US10806352's cardiovascular focus teaches away from CSF-specific applications. However, these are not strong teaching-away arguments.

C2_survival_assessment.rationale: The §103 combination attack is stronger than initially assessed. US8870787 + US10413710 + US10806352 + eShunt anatomy addresses 4 of 6 claim limitations with moderate motivation. However, CL5 (temporal signature classification) remains unaddressed by any combination. C2's defensible novelty increasingly narrows to: (1) the temporal signature algorithm for obstruction detection, and (2) the specific combination of endovascular eShunt + differential CSF-venous pressure + temporal classification. The §103 attack is not complete — additional references from the 106 backward citations of US8870787 have not been fully analyzed.
C2_survival_assessment.what_would_kill_C2: Finding a reference that teaches temporal pattern classification of pressure signals for distinguishing shunt obstruction from confounders (posture, cough, drift). If such a reference exists in the remaining 90+ unanalyzed citations, C2's defensible novelty narrows further.
C2_survival_assessment.what_would_save_C2: Confirming that no reference in the complete citation network teaches temporal signature classification for shunt obstruction detection. If CL5 survives, C2 has a defensible inventive step.
C2_survival_assessment.gate_state_after: YELLOW (SURVIVAL PLAUSIBLE, ATTACK INCOMPLETE — 106 citations found, 4 analyzed, 102 remaining)

scheduler_policy_update.old_policy: SCIENTIFIC_FIRST — always execute highest SCIENTIFIC_AQ first
scheduler_policy_update.new_policy: Per CEO Round 140: 'Use truth-first as a promotion constraint, but allow decision-value experiments to influence resource allocation when two scientific actions are close.'

implementation.promotion_constraint: Scientific truth is mandatory for WORLD_CLASS_INVENTION. No amount of decision-value evidence can substitute.
implementation.scheduling_rule: When two experiments have similar SCIENTIFIC_AQ (within 20%), choose the one with higher DECISION_AQ. When SCIENTIFIC_AQ differs by >20%, always choose the higher SCIENTIFIC_AQ regardless of DECISION_AQ.
implementation.rationale: Truth-first for promotion. Balanced for scheduling. The machine never says 'commercially valuable therefore mechanism confidence rises.' But it can say 'both experiments have similar scientific value; choose the one that resolves the more consequential portfolio decision.'
